h1: Everybody Knows Who to Ask. Only She Knows the Answer.
seo_title: How to Share Company Knowledge Beyond One Employee | NATA
meta_description: Capture how experts recognize exceptions, show staff where the answer applies, and test whether someone else can use it.
section_questions: What knowledge is worth writing down first?
What should a useful knowledge entry contain?
How do you know someone else can use the guidance?
answer_capsule: To make company knowledge usable beyond one person, start with a decision people regularly bring to that expert. Capture the facts they check, why those facts matter, when the guidance applies, and when someone must escalate. Put it where the next employee works and test it on real examples.
takeaways: It says what someone can decide and which facts they need.
It is available at the point where they will decide.
It shows where the standard answer ends and who can take over.

faqs.question: Should every expert conversation be recorded?
faqs.answer: Capture recurring decisions and meaningful exceptions first. Check permission and keep only information the next employee needs. A short, maintained entry will often be easier to use than a full recording.

faqs.question: Can a search assistant replace the knowledge owner?
faqs.answer: It can help find an approved answer. Someone still needs to maintain the source, define where it applies, and handle exceptions that require a decision.

faqs.question: What should happen to outdated guidance?
faqs.answer: Remove it from the active path and preserve history where the business needs it. Point readers to the current version and show who can confirm uncertain cases.
